title: Cheese bread puffs
summary: A low-carb take on Brazilian pão de queijo: small golden puffs of almond flour, egg, cream cheese and parmesan.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F) and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Whisk the almond flour, psyllium, baking powder and salt.
Beat the cream cheese, parmesan, eggs, olive oil and garlic together, then stir in the dry ingredients to make a thick, sticky dough. Rest 5 minutes.
With wet hands, roll into 12 balls about 3 cm (1¼ in) across and space them on the sheet.
Bake 18–22 minutes, until puffed and golden. Eat warm.

swaps.note: There is no dairy-free parmesan in this book; a smaller amount of extra almond flour keeps the dough's texture.

dairy_free_notes: The dairy-free version holds together and bakes up the same, but it is honestly a savoury almond puff, not a cheese bread — the parmesan supplies the flavour. Add a pinch more salt and garlic.
tips: Traditional pão de queijo gets its stretch from tapioca starch, which this version leaves out; expect a soft, tender crumb instead.

origin.history: Pão de queijo comes from Minas Gerais in Brazil, where it is made from tapioca (cassava) starch and local cured cheese, giving a crisp shell and a chewy, stretchy middle. Its roots are usually traced to the region's colonial era; it became a national snack in the twentieth century. This recipe is a low-carb take that replaces the tapioca with almond flour.
